proof_summary: Writing the binomial step from \(m=p^{r-1}\) to \(q=p^r\) as a product over the \(p\)-units and pairing \(k\) with \(q-k\) gives \(\binom{(c+1)q}{q}/\binom{(c+1)m}{m}\equiv 1+c(c+1)q^2T\pmod{p^{3r+3}}\), where divisibility of the reciprocal sum \(T=\sum 1/(k(q-k))\) and of the quadratic symmetric sum follows from inversion symmetry, periodicity modulo \(p\), and the sum-of-squares formula. Substituting \(c=2,1\) makes the remaining correction factor through \(2\binom{3m}{m}^2-9\binom{2m}{m}\), which is divisible by \(p^3\) for \(p\ge5\) and by \(3^4\) for \(p=3\); together with \(q\mid T\) (respectively \(3^{r-1}\mid T\)), these valuations annihilate both the linear and quadratic corrections.
